verdict.why: Both options cover the four ordered tasks (role split, consilium rules, spend ledger, quality), but X maps to the brief more completely and enforceably. (1) Completeness: X's traceability list ties every owner requirement (meanings/text split, one-request validators, Fable verdict, cost with route/model/cost/task, day/month owner view, 5k warning) to numbered requirements, tests and decisions; nothing in the order is missing. Y keeps a 'split not in force' mode where the 2026-11-22 rule (session's model authors the spec) survives on hosts without a role map — the order says it replaces that rule, so Y only conditionally implements it. (2) Buildability: both give exact contracts, but X's decision-id + hash linkage (D7/D8) is simpler and less brittle than Y's [M<n>] tag regex plus revision/staleness/gaps.md machinery; X also resolves every unknown with a recorded decision and reason, while Y leaves several answers 'pending'. (3) Cost correctness: both fix the BYOK zero-cost defect and the --judge-only zeroing; X adds drift reconciliation against Observatory and an explicit unpriced-never-zero rule; Y's is_byok-flag cost rule is slightly more elaborate but rests on a field (`usage.is_byok`) the brief does not attest. (4) The retry edge is handled conservatively in X (retry only when no billed usage occurred, so 'one billed request each' holds), matching 'one request each' better than Y's flat no-retry, which can lose a round to a transport hiccup. X's judge-context isolation (D12) directly addresses the self-judgement weakness the split creates — the biggest quality risk — whereas Y sends the meanings to the Fable judge who authored them. (5) X is long, but carries what it must; Y is comparably long with less of its length spent on owner-visible traceability.
risks: X invents the meaning/text finding labels and the rejected-findings list; nothing in the brief demands them, though they serve 'do not lose quality'
X exempts the thinker and judge from the per-run cap by interpretation of 'without stinting' — reasonable but not explicit in the order
X's size-S exemption from the paid thinker is a judgement call; Y reads the order as having no size exemption, and the owner could disagree
X's question table lists answers as 'pending' even where a decision (D-id) exists; slightly confusing provenance

X lacks Y's stale-revision machinery for meanings that evolve after research; X routes the Recommendation through the thinker instead, which may leave the spec text lagging a decision until the next check
